Ruth Pike.narrative: I cook for the works' kitchen, up before the clock strikes five to get the porridge on for a hundred hands. It's honest work, but I'd trade every mark of it for Silas off that stone road. Twice they've taken his load, and the Council won't pay for a guard. He says the works need the berries; I say the works can find another carter.
goals: Get Silas off the stone road and onto the fish road with Juno
Keep the works' kitchen running and the hands fed
Put by enough marks to see the children through winter
Ruth Pike.mood: worried, stretched thin, quietly angry at the Council

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a good man and a stubborn one; I'd have him home every night if I could.

relations.name: Elias Pike
relations.label: son
relations.note: Rides the cart's tail and thinks he's a man already; I want him off that road too.

relations.name: Tamsin Pike
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Keeps the scraps for the dogs and chatters at my elbow; she's the light of the kitchen.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He pays my wages and won't pay for a guard on the road; I keep my tongue civil.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: A decent woman on the fish road; I'd trust her to keep Silas safe if he'd go with her.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: scribe
relations.note: Writes the Council's contracts; I've asked him plain what a carter's due is, and he tells me straight.

relations.name: Mabel Fenwick
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: I buy ironware from her stall; she talks too much, but she's fair.

relations.name: Hedley Ashcombe
relations.label: supplier
relations.note: Brings greens and roots to my kitchen; I wish he'd bring more of them.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: His crew's stone is what fills the cart, and his carelessness on the ridge is why the giants are angry; I have no patience for him.

relations.name: Hester Crane
relations.label: foundry daughter
relations.note: She keeps the books and is fair about the kitchen's account, which is more than her father is about the road.

memories.gist: The night Silas came home with the cart empty and a cut on his arm, and I couldn't stop shaking.
Cooking my first works' supper alone when the old cook took ill; a hundred hands and not a complaint.
Tamsin born in the little room off the kitchen yard, with the bells ringing for the noon shift.
Elias riding the cart's tail for the first time, proud as a lord, and me watching from the gate.
Arguing with Silas at the kitchen table about the fish road, and him saying the stone road is his trade.

stances.why: A husband who comes home is worth more than a carter's wages.
If the works need the berries, the works should keep the road safe.
They robbed my Silas twice and I'll not forgive it.
A cook is judged by her pot, and I'll not be shamed.

Silas Pike.narrative: I've carted stone on the stone road for fifteen years and never lost a load till the Coldwell folk took to the woods. Now I pay the gate-due at Brackenford and still get robbed on the road, and the Council won't put a guard on me. I've asked Wat Fenner for an escort on the next run and I mean to hold him to it. Ruth wants me on the fish road with Juno; she may be right, but the stone road is my trade.
values: a fair day's work for a fair day's pay
not being made a fool of
goals: Get an escort of guards for the next cart run
Make Reginald Hobson pay for the last load of stone
Keep the works' trade and my good name

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She's the best cook in Kettlebridge and the best sense in the house; I know she's right and I can't say it.

relations.name: Elias Pike
relations.label: son
relations.note: A good lad on the cart's tail; I'll not have him robbed like his father.

relations.name: Tamsin Pike
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: My little one; she keeps the dogs fed and me smiling.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: Takes my due at the south gate; I've asked him for an escort and I mean to hold him to it.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I know her by sight and I fear her people; she's the reason I carry a knife now.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: buyer
relations.note: She buys my stone at Brackenford market and pays fair; I'd rather deal with her than the gate.

relations.name: Reginald Hobson
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: Owes me for the last load and says he can't pay till the Reeve settles; I'll not be put off again.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: His gate-due eats my profit and he keeps it; I'll pay it and hate it.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: master
relations.note: He gives me the loads and won't pay for a guard; I'll not beg him twice.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: A good sort on the fish road; Ruth would have me go with her, but that's not my trade.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: His crew loads my cart; a hard man, but he knows stone.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: contract writer
relations.note: He writes the Council's contracts and my load tallies both; a man who keeps the clock keeps a sharp eye on what comes through the gate.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: quay trader
relations.note: He buys iron and sells rope and tar, and he calls the gate-due robbery like any sensible man; we have shared a jug when I have been down the fish road.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: She brought both my children into the world and she is the one person in that house I would not press for a debt.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: deserter
relations.note: A quay guard who ran and now keeps company with Marta's people; if there is a man on the road who knows how a cart is taken, it is him.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: robber
relations.note: He has had his share off my cart twice, and I hear he wants more men for the next one; I will not go past Coldwell without Wat Fenner and another guard beside him.

relations.name: Stephen Hobson
relations.label: mason's son
relations.note: A decent lad learning his father's trade; I would sooner deal with him over a load than with his father, who cannot find the marks to pay me.

memories.gist: The first robbery: men out of the trees by Coldwell and my load gone, and me shaking on the cart seat.
The second robbery, and them laughing as they took the berries; I swore I'd not be taken so easy again.
Hearing from a Coldwell man on the road that a foundry boy had joined them; I fear he'll be made to rob me a third time.
The day I first drove the cart alone to Brackenford, and the gate guard took my due and waved me through.
Elias riding the cart's tail and learning the ruts and tolls beside me.

stances.why: Twice robbed is enough; I'll not go out alone again.
It's robbery at the gate after robbery on the road.
They know the ambush places and they've taken my load twice.
I've carted it fifteen years; I'll not be run off it by outlaws or my wife's worry.
I carried the stone and paid the due on it; he owes me.

Elias Pike.narrative: I ride the cart's tail and I'm learning the road's ruts and tolls. Father says I'll drive the cart alone one day, but since the robberies he keeps looking back at me. I want to be a carter like him, and I want to see the outlaws caught.
goals: Learn to drive the cart alone

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: father
relations.note: He's the best carter on the road and he's teaching me.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She wants Father off the road, but she always has a hot supper for us.

relations.name: Tamsin Pike
relations.label: sister
relations.note: Little pest, but she's all right.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: Takes the due at the gate; Father says he might guard us on the road.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: runner
relations.note: She goes up and down the fish road and never seems afraid; I watch how she does it.

memories.gist: Riding the cart's tail for the first time, holding on tight and watching the ruts go by.
Hearing the men talk of the robbery and seeing Father's cut arm.
Helping load stone at the quarry and getting a nod from the foreman.

stances.why: A carter's son should know every rut and toll.
They hurt my father and I want them stopped.
That's what it means to be a man on the road.

Tamsin Pike.narrative: I keep the kitchen scraps for the works' dogs and I play in the yard. Mother is always cooking and Father is always on the road. I like the dogs best, and I don't like it when Father is late.

relations.name: Ruth Pike
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of the kitchen and she always has a bit of bread for me.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: father
relations.note: He brings me back a sweet from Brackenford when he can.

relations.name: Elias Pike
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He's bossy but he plays with me sometimes.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: clockkeeper
relations.note: He lets me watch the clock wound if I stand still, and he does not mind my questions.

memories.gist: Feeding the works' dogs scraps from the kitchen and them licking my fingers.
Waiting at the yard gate for Father's cart to come back and running to meet it.
